_fixture_note: EXAMPLE DATA ONLY. This file is hand-written so the publish stage can be built and tested before the real pipeline produces output. The council and topic are real; the documents, dates, quotes and summaries below are illustrative and must never be published as fact. The figures below are illustrative too.

council.name: Norwich City Council
council.remit_note: Norwich City Council runs licensing, planning, council housing, bins and street cleaning, and environmental health for the city. It does not run roads, schools, social care or libraries — those belong to Norfolk County Council. So if a licensing decision affects traffic or parking on a street, two different councils are involved.

topic.name: Licensing policy
topic.plain_english: The rules the council uses when it decides who can sell alcohol, open late, or put on live music — and what conditions it can attach to keep noise and disorder down.

questions.asked: Residents living near Prince of Wales Road and in the Golden Triangle asked for tighter controls on late-opening venues, mainly because of noise and street disorder after midnight. Some businesses and the trade association asked for the opposite: fewer blanket restrictions and more case-by-case decisions.
questions.decided: The council adopted a new five-year licensing policy in January 2025. It kept a special “cumulative impact” area covering Prince of Wales Road, added a new agent-of-change condition for venues near homes, but did not extend the special area into the Golden Triangle as residents there had asked.
questions.done: The policy was published and took effect in March 2025. The promised review of how the cumulative impact area is working has not been published yet, so we do not know whether anything changed on the ground.

sources.title: Consultation: draft Statement of Licensing Policy 2025–2030
sources.summary: The council asked the public what it should change in its licensing policy for the next five years. The consultation ran for eight weeks in summer 2024 and asked specifically about late-night opening hours, the existing special area on Prince of Wales Road, and noise from venues near homes.

sources.title: Consultation responses report: draft Statement of Licensing Policy
sources.summary: The officers' report counts and groups the 412 responses. Most residents who replied wanted tighter controls after midnight, especially near Prince of Wales Road and in the Golden Triangle. Licensed businesses and the local trade association argued that blanket restrictions punish well-run venues and asked for decisions to be made case by case.

sources.title: Licensing Committee minutes, 19 November 2024
sources.summary: The Licensing Committee went through the consultation responses and agreed what to recommend to Full Council. It kept the Prince of Wales Road special area, added a new condition for venues near homes, and turned down the request to extend the special area into the Golden Triangle because it said the evidence on crime and noise there was not strong enough.

sources.title: Full Council minutes, 28 January 2025
sources.summary: Full Council formally adopted the Statement of Licensing Policy 2025–2030 as recommended by the Licensing Committee. The minutes record that councillors also asked officers to report back within twelve months on whether the special area is working.

sources.title: Statement of Licensing Policy 2025–2030 (published)
sources.summary: The final policy document now in force. It sets out the cumulative impact area on Prince of Wales Road, the hours the council will normally grant, and the new condition requiring new venues near homes to show how they will manage noise.

sources.title: Licensing Committee agenda, 17 June 2025
sources.summary: This agenda is the most recent Licensing Committee paper we could find. It does not contain the twelve-month review of the cumulative impact area that Full Council asked for in January 2025.

events.title: The council asked people what should change in its licensing rules
events.summary: Norwich City Council opened an eight-week public consultation on a new licensing policy to run from 2025 to 2030. It asked residents and businesses about late-night opening hours, the existing special area on Prince of Wales Road, and noise affecting people who live near venues.
detail: Ran online, with paper copies at City Hall and the Forum

events.title: Most residents who replied asked for tighter control of late-night venues
events.summary: Of 412 responses, the officers' report says the largest group was residents living near Prince of Wales Road and in the Golden Triangle. They asked the council to keep the existing special area, to be slower to grant hours past midnight, and to do more about noise and litter from people leaving venues.
detail: Most common request: no new licences past 01:00 near housing
Second most common: extend the special area into the Golden Triangle

events.title: Licensed businesses asked for fewer blanket rules and more case-by-case decisions
events.summary: Licence holders and a trade association argued that a special area penalises well-run venues alongside badly-run ones. They asked the council to judge each application on its own evidence rather than applying an area-wide presumption against new licences. The responses report does not give an exact date for these submissions, so we only know the month.

events.title: The Licensing Committee kept the Prince of Wales Road special area and added a noise condition
events.summary: The committee agreed to recommend the new policy to Full Council. It kept the cumulative impact area on Prince of Wales Road, citing the consultation responses and police data, and added a condition requiring new venues near homes to set out how they will manage noise.
detail: Cumulative impact area on Prince of Wales Road: kept
New “agent of change” noise condition: added

events.title: The committee turned down the request to extend the special area into the Golden Triangle
events.summary: Residents had asked for the cumulative impact area to cover the Golden Triangle as well. The committee did not agree, recording that the crime and nuisance evidence for that area did not meet the legal test for a cumulative impact assessment.

events.title: Full Council adopted the policy and asked for a review within twelve months
events.summary: Councillors formally adopted the Statement of Licensing Policy 2025–2030. The minutes also record a request for officers to report back within twelve months on whether the cumulative impact area is having any effect.

events.title: The new policy was published and took effect
events.summary: The Statement of Licensing Policy 2025–2030 was published on the council's website and applies to licence applications from 1 March 2025. The new noise condition for venues near homes is in the published text.

events.title: The twelve-month review of the special area has not been published
events.summary: Full Council asked for a report within twelve months on whether the cumulative impact area is working. We checked Licensing Committee agendas up to June 2025 and could not find it. We do not know whether it has been written and not published, or not written at all.

events.title: Whether late-night noise complaints have changed is not published
events.summary: The point of the policy is to reduce noise and disorder near homes. We looked for published complaint or licensing-enforcement figures for Prince of Wales Road before and after March 2025 and did not find any. Without those numbers nobody can say whether the policy has made a difference.

linkages.evidence: Members noted that the majority of consultation responses supported retention of the cumulative impact area and agreed that this, together with the police evidence, justified its retention.
linkages.explanation: The committee's own minutes say the consultation responses were part of why it kept the special area, so the council has recorded the link itself.

linkages.evidence: The committee considered the request from residents to extend the cumulative impact area to the Golden Triangle but concluded the available evidence did not meet the statutory test.
linkages.explanation: The minutes name the residents' request and explain why it was turned down — a confirmed link, even though the answer was no.
Residents asked for a way to check the special area actually works, and Full Council asked for a twelve-month review — but the minutes do not say the two are connected, so we cannot claim they are.
The businesses' request for case-by-case decisions instead of an area-wide rule is not mentioned anywhere in the committee's recorded reasons, so we found no link.

gaps.description: We could not find the individual consultation responses, only the officers' summary of them. So we are relying on the council's own count of what people said rather than reading it ourselves.
There is no published record of how each councillor voted on the licensing policy. The minutes record the decision but not a recorded vote.
We looked for the twelve-month review of the cumulative impact area on Licensing Committee agendas up to June 2025 and could not find it.

We looked for published noise-complaint or licensing-enforcement figures for Prince of Wales Road before and after March 2025 and found none, so the effect of the policy cannot be measured from public data.

figures.label: Responses to the consultation
figures.note: Counted in the officers' report. It does not say how many were from residents and how many from businesses.

figures.label: Wanted tighter control of late-night venues
figures.note: Share of the 412 responses, as grouped by officers. People could pick more than one theme, so the shares do not add to 100.

figures.label: How long the policy runs before it must be redone
figures.note: Set by the Licensing Act 2003, not by the council.

figures.label: Cost of running the licensing service
figures.note: Budgeted, not spent. The out-turn figure for the year has not been published.

figures.label: Date the policy took effect
figures.note: The council published it on the same day it came into force.

measures.question: Did the council get its new licensing rules out on time?
measures.label: New licensing policy published before the old one ran out
measures.rule: Met if a later council report says the dated commitment was delivered. Close if a later report says it was delivered late or only in part. Missed if a later report says it was dropped, or that something other than the promise was delivered. Can't tell if no later report addresses it.

target.display: A new policy in force before the 2020–2025 one expired

actual.display: Published and in force from 1 March 2025

measures.evidence: The law says a licensing policy has to be replaced every five years. The council published its new one on 1 March 2025, before the old one ran out.

promises.question: Did the council do the review it promised within a year?
promises.label: Twelve-month review of the Prince of Wales Road special area
promises.rule: Met if a later council report says the dated commitment was delivered. Close if a later report says it was delivered late or only in part. Missed if a later report says it was dropped, or that something other than the promise was delivered. Can't tell if no later report addresses it.

target.display: “A review of the special policy area within twelve months”, agreed 28 January 2025

actual.display: No later report we can find says whether the review happened.

promises.evidence: When it adopted the policy, the council promised to look again at the Prince of Wales Road area within a year. Nothing published since says whether it did.
promises.looked_for: A committee report, minute or published review dated on or after January 2026.
